questions.question: A user clicks an item but never rates it. Which signal type is that click?
options: Implicit feedback
An explicit rating
A confirmed negative preference
A held-out target by definition
questions.explanation: A click records an observed action, not a stated rating. It also does not prove that the user disliked every unclicked item.

questions.question: For an interaction matrix, what does popularity_scores count for each item in the scratch code?
options: The average rating including missing entries as zero
The number of users with a positive interaction for that item
The item index multiplied by its price
The number of latent factors in the model
questions.explanation: The implementation counts rows where the item value is greater than zero, giving a simple popularity baseline.

questions.question: A user has two relevant held-out items and the recommender places one of them in its top-3 list. What is Recall@3?
questions.explanation: Recall@3 is relevant items retrieved divided by all held-out relevant items: 1/2=0.5.

questions.question: Why does leave_one_out remove an observed item from a user's training row?
options: It turns every observed item into a negative label
It guarantees that popularity is the best method
It removes the user from the factorization entirely
It creates a held-out relevant item for leakage-safe ranking evaluation
questions.explanation: The removed interaction acts as a held-out relevant item; recommendations are made from the remaining history and then compared with it.

questions.question: A brand-new user has no interaction history. Which fallback does the demo expose?
options: Recommend the most popular items
Recommend items the user already clicked
Fit a personal factor vector from zero observations
Return every item in random order
questions.explanation: Popularity does not require a user history, so it is a practical cold-start fallback in the artifact.

questions.question: What is a main limitation of an item list ranked only by popularity?
options: It cannot rank items for a user without explicit ratings
It can reinforce exposure bias and hide less popular but relevant items
It always produces a personalized ranking
It evaluates NDCG without needing a held-out set
questions.explanation: Popularity reflects prior exposure as well as preference, so a popularity-only list can become self-reinforcing and less diverse.
